title: Oxygen — Crew Oxygen Cylinder Cradle and Pressure Transducer Replacement
abstract: Replacement of the bourdon-tube pressure transducer by a temperature-compensated solid-state item and rework of the cylinder cradle saddle, ending the unnecessary cylinder changes caused by gauge drift.

sections.planning_reason: The transducer fitted at build drifts with temperature and ages by about two per cent a year, which puts an in-tolerance cylinder below the dispatch line on a cold morning. Forty-three of sixty-one cylinders returned in an eighteen-month sample were within limits when tested. Each unnecessary change is a two-hour job in the flight compartment with the crew rest floor lifted, and three operators reported delayed departures. A secondary finding was cradle strap chafe on the cylinder neck at high-cycle operators.
sections.description: The transducer is replaced by a solid-state item with a temperature-compensated output and the indicating channel is re-ranged to suit. The non-return valve at the cylinder outlet is renewed because it must be disturbed. The cradle is reworked so that the strap bears on a moulded saddle rather than directly on the cylinder neck, and the charging pump connection is relocated fifty millimetres outboard to give tool clearance at the transducer.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Do AMM-S-35-10-11-800-038-A to depressurise the crew oxygen system and confirm zero pressure at the charging point. WARNING: OXYGEN. NO OIL, NO GREASE, NO SMOKING WITHIN FIFTEEN METRES. MAKE SURE ALL TOOLS AND HANDS ARE FREE OF HYDROCARBON. Lift the crew rest floor panel and do AMM-S-35-10-11-000-039-A to remove the cylinder. Remove the transducer and the non-return valve. Install the non-return valve D3510118104447 and the solid-state transducer, and lock-wire both. Rework the cradle to accept the moulded saddle and fit the saddle. Relocate the charging pump connection YS788350-31 fifty millimetres outboard. Re-install the cylinder and torque the strap to the value in the accomplishment instructions. Re-range the indicating channel and do a leak check at working pressure with a soap solution. Charge the cylinder and record the indicated pressure against the reference gauge at two temperatures.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to aircraft from MSN S00029 to MSN S01232 fitted with the bourdon-tube transducer. Aircraft from MSN S01430 onward are post-modification from build. The four-engine aircraft are not covered because their cradle attaches to a different floor structure.
sections.material_note: Kit K3510-1005-01 contains the transducer, the non-return valve, the moulded saddle and the relocation bracket. Lead time is twelve weeks. The removed transducer is returned to Aeralis for drift measurement so that the fleet ageing model stays current.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled A-check, or within 24 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
